drg.description: Kidney and Urinary Tract Infections without MCC

notes.text:
HISTORY AND PHYSICAL. Chart, labs and overnight events reviewed. 49-year-old male admitted for urinary tract infection. Admission data:
Day 0: labs bilirubin 0.48, creatinine 0.72, hemoglobin 14.2, platelets 241, sodium 134, wbc 8.1; vitals dbp 67-72, heart_rate 83-87, map 90-94, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 14-15, sbp 133-138, spo2 95-97, temp 36.8-37
Day 0 orders/meds/results: Urinalysis: positive nitrites, >50 WBC/hpf; Ceftriaxone 1 g IV
Assessment and plan: Urinary tract infection. Sodium mildly low, not clinically significant.

PROGRESS NOTE, hospital day 1. Chart, labs and overnight events reviewed. Data:
Day 1: labs creatinine 0.71, hemoglobin 13.9, platelets 243, sodium 139, wbc 8.6; vitals dbp 67-72, heart_rate 84-89, map 89-94, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 14-15, sbp 133-139, spo2 95-96, temp 36.8-37.1
Day 1 orders/meds/results: Ceftriaxone 1 g IV
Assessment and plan: Urinary tract infection. Sodium mildly low, not clinically significant. Continue current management.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY. 49-year-old male, length of stay 2 days. Hospital course: treated per the plan above with daily labs and vital signs; stable for discharge. Medications reconciled and return precautions reviewed. Discharge diagnoses: Urinary tract infection. Sodium mildly low, not clinically significant. Follow up with primary care in one week. Chart, labs and overnight events reviewed.
